evidence.source: 趙立偉, “由出土文獻看草、早、皂記詞功能的更替與用法分工”
evidence.field: abstract; dating and use of excavated graphs
evidence.text: The 2020 article (冬季號, pp. 117–130) reports that oracle-bone 草 was used as a phonetic loan for the word 早; Qin-series slips use the graph 早 for a word related to 皂 rather than for “early”; and Han frontier slips add a left-falling stroke to 早 to form 皁, after which 皁 takes over a “black” use. This account complicates the dossier’s inference that oracle-bone 早 already meant “morning.” The accessible page provides only the abstract, so the specific artifacts, contexts, and dating ranges behind the conclusions could not be checked here.
evidence.title: 由出土文獻看草、早、皂記詞功能的更替與用法分工

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫, entry 早
evidence.field: 形義通解; graphic analyses and attested spellings
evidence.text: The database presents two analyses: early bronze forms as 日 plus 甲, interpreted as the sun’s initial appearance and the morning period; later bronze forms as 日 plus 棗, with 棗 sometimes reduced to 朿, analyzed as phonosemantic. It also records manuscript/classical borrowing of 蚤 for 早, citing a Mawangdui Warring States text (“君之封地不可不蚤定”) and the Mencius (“蚤起”), and 棗 for 早 in Shuihudi Qin slips (“利棗不利莫”). These are distinct claims about a graph’s structure and about which graph wrote which word; the cited forms do not by themselves settle the first use of the spoken word “early.”
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 字頭「早」

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫, entry 早
evidence.text: The entry quotes the Han-era Shuowen Jiezi gloss “晨也。从日在甲上” (“morning; from 日 with 甲 above”) and records the Guangyun fanqie 子晧, Middle Chinese category 精母, 上聲, 豪/皓 rhyme, 開口一等. It treats Xu Shen’s explanation as an account of the seal-script form and also supplies a distinct later-bronze phonosemantic account.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 字頭「早」

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫, entry 棗
evidence.field: 形義通解; 《說文》; Shuihudi slip citation
evidence.text: The database analyzes 棗 as two stacked 朿 components, associated with a thorny jujube tree, and quotes Shuowen: “棗，羊棗也。从重朿.” It separately reports 棗 read for 早, ‘morning,’ in Shuihudi Qin slip 日書甲種, slip 14 recto: “利棗(早)不利莫(暮).” Thus the character 棗 has an independently described plant referent and a documented loan use for the word 早; its plant-name pronunciation need not be inferred from the pronoun analysis.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 字頭「棗」

evidence.source: 謝小麗, “秦簡中關於‘早’的一組同義詞辨析”
evidence.field: section 蚤（早）; dated publication and cited manuscript examples
evidence.text: The 2013 article (published 2013-05-30) says Qin slips use 蚤 for 早, in opposition to 暮 and also in the expressions 蚤至 and 蚤食, citing Shuihudi and other Qin slips. It quotes Shuowen’s “早，晨也。从日在甲上” and Guangyun’s statement that 蚤 was an ancient loan for early/dusk words. This supports an early writing practice distinct from graphic origin; it does not claim that the oracle-bone form of 早 itself is securely attested for the morning word.
evidence.title: 謝小麗：秦簡中關於“早”的一組同義詞辨析

evidence.source: 教育部《異體字字典》, entry A01773 早
evidence.field: 說文釋形; 字樣說明; senses
evidence.text: The Taiwan Ministry of Education entry gives Shuowen’s analysis “晨也。从日在甲上” and explains the regular form’s lower 十 as a transformation of seal-script 甲. It lists senses including dawn/morning, events in the morning, earlier than a scheduled time, earlier/initial, and an adverbial ‘already.’ This is an organized gloss inventory, not evidence that the senses arose in that order.
evidence.title: 教育部《異體字字典》 A01773 早

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫, entry 早
evidence.field: 形義通解; dated bronze inscription example
evidence.text: The database cites the later-bronze inscription 中山王鼎 “早棄羣臣” in support of 早 used with the sense ‘early/sooner,’ while its broader discussion distinguishes this later phonosemantic form from the 日+甲 analysis. The page does not give a specific calendar date for this inscription in the accessible entry, so no tighter dating is asserted here.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 字頭「早」

Compared within the same system to 早 *Nə.tsˤuʔ, these forms are related in their reconstructed segmental material but not identical; this is a phonological comparison, not proof that 棗 was the historical phonetic in a particular inscription. evidence.text: Exact local row: 蚤, Mandarin zǎo, MC tsawX, OC *tsˤuʔ, gloss “flea” (GSR 1112d). Its comparison with 早 *Nə.tsˤuʔ is within Baxter–Sagart notation. evidence.text: Exact local row: 皁, Mandarin zào, MC dzawX, OC *[dz]ˤuʔ, gloss “acorn, black-dyeing fruit” (GSR 1054b). This is distinct from 早 *Nə.tsˤuʔ and 棗 *[ts]ˤuʔ in the same table. The row documents the table’s lexical reading and gloss, but cannot establish that an ancient 早-shaped graph depicted an acorn or that the depicted object was pronounced like the borrowed word. gaps: The TOAJ publisher provides an abstract but its linked full-text PDF was inaccessible; the artifact-level evidence and chronology underlying its oracle-bone 草 → 早 and Qin/Han use claims therefore remain unchecked.

The origin of the proposed early acorn/皂 pictograph is disputed and not independently established here. A B–S reconstruction for the pronoun 早 does not establish the ancient name or pronunciation of an acorn; the object-to-word sound basis for that specific whole-graph loan remains unverified.

The dossier's 棗 phonetic account is supported as an analysis of later bronze forms by CUHK and the imported secondary account, but exact inscription images and a securely dated earliest example were not visually inspected. CUHK additionally reports a separate 日+甲 interpretation for bronze forms; the disagreement is not fully resolved.

The modern and B–S local readings of candidate component/host characters 棗, 蚤 and 皁 were inspected, but official Unicode character-specific pages for their codepoints could not be accessed. Accordingly the local rows are identified as local evidence and not passed off as external verification.
Baxter–Sagart exact rows for 枣 (simplified 棗), 皂, and other possible hosts were not established from the inspected rows. No host sound reading is inferred from 早.

The local glyph lead for 早 was not visually inspected in this pass; no claim about the exact pictured glyph, its provenance, or license is made. No reusable corpus extract is recommended: the inspected sites provide character-specific scholarly content, and no explicit reuse terms sufficient to justify a local extract were verified.

No chronology is inferred from dictionary gloss order. “Earlier/initial,” “already,” and other extensions appear in dictionary inventories, but the inspected evidence does not establish their chronological paths from the morning sense.

The TOAJ full-text PDF was linked but not accessible during this pass; artifact-level details behind its oracle-bone 草 → 早 and Qin/Han 草/早/皁 chronology remain unchecked. It conflicts with analyses assigning early 早 forms to the morning word, so the disagreement remains unresolved.
CUHK confirms a later-bronze 日+棗 phonosemantic analysis and an alternate 日+甲 analysis, but the exact inscription images were not viewable in this pass and their dating was not independently verified.

The accessible CUHK evidence documents 蚤 and 棗 as whole-graph loan spellings for the word 早. It does not independently establish the earliest attestation or chronological semantic path of the spoken word ‘early.’

No candidate historical glyph image met the required verified identity and reuse-provenance checks: exact Commons pages failed to open, and CUHK image endpoints provided no usable image content or specific rights notice. No image selected.
Current and Baxter–Sagart component readings in the supplied local rows were not rechecked through character-specific upstream records in this pass; no new phonetic-reading claim is made.
